newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INTER TOP IN ITALY, NEWCASTLE IN ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER TOP IN ITALY, NEWCASTLE IN ENGLAND.

text.p: Internazionale Milan moved clear at the top in Italy with a 1-0 win over Verona and Newcastle replaced Arsenal as leaders of the English premier league, beating Middlesbrough 3-1.
A round-up of this weekend's major soccer league action in Europe:
Italy

Argentine Javier Zanetti scored five minutes from the end to give Inter a 1-0 win at Verona on Sunday and a one-point lead at the top of serie A as title rivals AC Milan and Juventus were both held to home draws.
Juventus drew 1-1 with Napoli and champions Milan needed a second-half penalty from Demetrio Albertini to salvage a point against Atalanta in the San Siro stadium.

Inter, taken to a penalty shoot-out before eliminating Austria's Graz from the UEFA Cup last week, lead serie A with 17 points from eight matches. They are one ahead of Vicenza, who won 2-0 away to Lazio, and two clear of Juventus.
England

Newcastle captain Peter Beardsley celebrated his 700th league and cup appearance with two goals in his team's 3-1 derby win over Middlesbrough on Sunday which put them back on top of the premier league.
Robert Lee added Newcastle's third in the 75th minute as Kevin Keegan's team bounced back from a 2-0 defeat at Leicester eight days ago.
They leapfrogged two points clear of Arsenal, who drew 2-2 at Wimbledon on Saturday, and moved four points clear of third-placed Liverpool, who lost 3-0 to Blackburn earlier on Sunday.
The troubles of Manchester United continued with a 2-1 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday, the third premier league loss in succession for the reigning champions.
Germany
VfB Stuttgart missed the chance to overtake Bayern Munich at the top on Saturday when they suffered a surprise 2-1 defeat at lowly St Pauli.

Midfielder Christian Springer scored both goals for the unfashionable Hamburg side while Stuttgart's feared striking force made most of the play but managed only a penalty, converted by Bulgaria's Krasimir Balakov.
The defeat left Stuttgart, the 1992 champions, in second place on 27 points from 13 matches, one point behind Bayern, who drew 1-1 with local rivals 1860 Munich on Friday.
Spain
Real Madrid cut Barcelona's lead at the top to one point on Sunday after an unimpressive 2-1 victory at struggling Compostela.
With 25 points from 11 games, Real are second on goal difference just ahead of Deportivo Coruna, 2-1 winners at Zaragoza.
Barcelona did not play at the weekend. They are away to Sporting Gijon on Monday.
France
Paris St Germain restored their three-point lead with a 3-0 win over Bastia on Sunday, Panama striker Julio Cesar Dely scoring twice.

PSG, who routed Galatasaray in the European Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday, went ahead through Patrice Loko in the eighth minute. Dely Valdes missed two chances before the interval but confounded his critics with goals in the 71st and 81st minutes.
Two goals by teenager Thierry Henry had helped Monaco crush Bordeaux 3-1 on Saturday, taking them to the top for 24 hours on goal difference.
Netherlands
The three main contenders -- PSV Eindhoven, Feyenoord and Ajax Amsterdam -- all won away on Sunday.
Ajax beat Willem II Tilburg 1-0 and moved up to third but still trail leaders PSV by seven points.
PSV, eliminated from the European Cup Winners' Cup by Norway's Brann Bergen on Thursday, came from behind to beat Twente Enschede 2-1. Feyenoord won 1-0 at Groningen.
PSV lead the table with 33 points from 14 games, followed by Feyenoord with 32 and Ajax with 26 points.
Portugal
Reigning champions Porto extended their lead to four points with a 2-0 home win over Farense 2-0 on Sunday.
Porto, who beat Norway's Rosenborg 3-0 on Wednesday to guarantee a place in the last eight of the European Cup, lead with 23 points from nine matches.
Benfica, joint second with Sporting Lisbon, can reduce the gap when they face Boavista on Monday.
